claims.explanation: From \(y=x\), the argument is \(x+\frac{x}{x}=x+1\), not \(2x\). The correct simplification is \(f(x+1)=f(x)+1+2x\).

claims.quoted_text: the only solution that satisfies the original equation for all \(x, y \in \mathbb{Q}^+\) is when \(a = 2\) and \(b = 0\). Hence, \(f(x) = 2x\).
claims.explanation: This is false: \(f(x)=2x\) does not satisfy the equation, since the left side is \(2x+\frac{2y}{x}\) while the right side is \(2x+\frac{y}{x}+2y\). A valid solution is \(f(x)=x^2\), not \(2x\).

claims.quoted_text: the only possible value for \(f \left( \frac{1}{3} \right)\) based on the given conditions is \(\boxed{\frac{2}{3}}\)
claims.explanation: The final value is wrong. Using the corrected recurrence and setting \(x=\frac13, y=1\) gives \(f\left(\frac{1}{3}+3\right)=f\left(\frac13\right)+\frac{1}{f\left(\frac13\right)}+2\), while the recurrence gives \(f\left(\frac13+3\right)=f\left(\frac13\right)+11\), so \(f\left(\frac13\right)=\frac19\), not \(\frac23\).
